newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-FRENCH COACH JACQUET PLANS EXPERIMENT AGAINST ENGLAND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FRENCH COACH JACQUET PLANS EXPERIMENT AGAINST ENGLAND.

text.p: MONTPELLIER, France, June 6 - French coach Aime Jacquet will experiment with three strikers including Karlsruhe's Marc Keller, who scored the equaliser in the 1-1 draw with Brazil, for Saturday's Tournoi de France match against England.

Keller will make his first start in his fifth international, alongside Christophe Dugarry of AC Milan and Espanyol's Nicolas Ouedec, two players very much on trial for roles as strikers in the 1998 World Cup squad.

Jacquet sees Keller as a deep-lying forward able to help the midfield set up attacks in the manner of other players in the squad such as Ibrahim Ba on the right and Robert Pires, who are not included after starting against Brazil.
The strikers will play in front of Internazionale's Youri Djorkaeff, who replaces Zinedine Zidane, not at his Juventus best against the Brazilians.
"I am looking at a line-up I have only tried out once. I want to do it now because I won't have many other opportunities to do so in the future," Jacquet said.
"I wanted to do it earlier in the season but that was impossible because of injuries and other problems.

"To face England, you must have a physically fit team. Against Brazil we faced virtuosos. Against England it's going to be a fight. We know their game despite Glen Hoddle's efforts to make them play differently."

The new line-up also allows Jacquet to try out a three-man defence, dropping left back Bixente Lizarazu to make way for the extra forward, while Paris St Germain's Bruno N'Gotty replaces Marcel Desailly in central defence.
It also means extra ball-winning capacity in midfield which Jacquet hopes will come from Sampdoria's Pierre Laigle who will play alongside captain Didier Deschamps and Arsenal's Patrick Vieira.
The only sure thing about the England team is that it will be different from the one that defeated Italy 2-0 so convincingly in Nantes on Wednesday.

Hoddle's side is more likely to resemble the one that beat Poland 2-0 last Saturday in Chorzow because the team that played Italy was an experimental one. He did not want to field his likely line-up against the Italians just four months before their World Cup qualifier in Rome in October.
There could be as many as six changes with David Seaman likely to return in goal in place of Tim Flowers.
Sol Campbell and Gary Neville could start in the backline in place of Martin Keown and Stuart Pearce, with David Batty and Paul Gascoigne replacing Graeme Le Saux and Paul Scholes in midfield.
In attack, Alan Shearer is expected to start in place of Ian Wright.

Hoddle is delighted to be taking part in this tournament and has stressed many times that he is looking to experiment in all three games ahead of what he hopes will be a return to France for the World Cup finals next year.
He is eager to give some of the younger players in his squad, such as Philip Neville and Scholes, as much experience as he can but wants to balance that with the creation of a solid, first-team unit.
"France are a very creative side and they have a lot to prove to their own fans before the World Cup," he said.

"But this is an important week for us as well. I've been pleased with the way we have played in our last two matches -- in very different circumstances -- and I hope we continue to do well against both France and Brazil."

England have won eight of the nine matches they have played since Hoddle took over from Terry Venables at the end of Euro 96 and have a good overall record against France, winning 15 of the 22 matches they have played since 1923.

But France have not lost at home against England for 48 years. Since England won a friendly 3-1 in Paris in 1949, France have beaten England 1-0 in a friendly in 1955, 5-2 in a European championship qualifier in 1963 and 2-0 in a friendly in 1984.
England have not lost an away game for almost four years -- so something looks set to give in Montpellier on Saturday night.
Teams:
France - Fabien Bartez; Lilian Thuram, Laurent Blanc, Bruno N'Gotty; Pierre Laigle, Didier Deschamps, Patrick Viera, Youri Djorkaeff; Marc Keller, Nicolas Ouedec, Christophe Dugarry.
England (probable) - David Seaman; Gary Neville, Gareth Southgate, Sol Campbell, David Batty, Paul Gascoigne, David Beckham, Paul Ince, Philip Neville, Alan Shearer, Teddy Sheringham.
